7: There are those who have a custom to recite verses beforehand, such as "Shome'a Tefillah" (He who hears prayer), etc. But one should not recite them, as it constitutes an interruption. So wrote Hagahot Maimoniyot in the second chapter of Hilchot Tefillah, and likewise wrote Mordechai in the first chapter of Berakhot, and it is obvious. Our teacher was precise to write: "But at Musaf and Minchah, if one wishes to recite verses, he may recite them"—that is to say, but at Ma'ariv, no. This is because even at Ma'ariv there is a commandment to juxtapose Geulah to Tefillah. And so wrote the Kol Bo in the name of the Ramban, and so it seems from the words of Tosafot in the first chapter of Berakhot.
